source_review.notes: Reviewed the original Adelson-Velskii/Landis record, MIT lecture and recitation, current Boost.Intrusive AVL source, GNU libavl, Cornell functional treatment, current OCaml height-balanced Set source, current ISO C++ ordering requirements, Rust BTreeMap documentation, and OpenJDK TreeMap source. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200. Classical AVL, height-balanced variants, and red-black/B-tree alternatives are scoped separately.

evidence: Checked null-height zero, leaf-height one, bf=left height minus right height, N(h), rotation regions, primitive rotation, repair path, and augmentation terminology.
Checked LL/RR/LR/RL names are interpreted under the stated sign convention.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Sources using null height -1 or the opposite balance sign are not mixed into the implementation convention.

evidence: Confirmed LL and RR traces use one primitive rotation and LR/RL use two while all roots become 20.
Reconstructed the main tree before deletion: sorted keys -1,0,1,2,5,6,9,10,11, root 9, height four, two rotations.
Confirmed deleting 10 returns TEN and leaves -1,0,1,2,5,6,9,11, root 1, height four, three cumulative rotations.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite rotation counts establish only the recorded traces.

evidence: Verified N(h)>=2N(h-2) yields exponential minimum nodes and logarithmic maximum height.
Verified left/right rotation preserves ordered regions A<x<B<y<C and exact reachability including the middle subtree.
Verified demoted-first then promoted metadata recomputation follows dependency order.
Verified insertion's first repair restores prior subtree height, while deletion may reduce height and propagate upward.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter does not promote the loose recurrence bound into an exact maximum-height formula.

evidence: Reviewed empty/singleton, root/internal rotations, all four orientations, child-balance equality, leaf/one/two-child deletion, immediate/deep successor, and cascading repair.
Reviewed stale/wrapped height, balance magnitude beyond two, parent/root reconnect, middle-subtree ownership, other augmentations, association/node identity, and iterator paths.
Reviewed sorted input, hostile comparator/depth/serialized shape, allocation/value/comparison failure, intrusive/pool ownership, concurrency publication, reclamation, and resource limits.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Valid AVL height does not bound total input, comparator cost, allocation, or request rate.

evidence: Independently checked global BST bounds, unique node identity/reachability, reachable count=size, true height=stored height, and absolute child-height difference at most one.
Checked update and every rotation/deletion preserve exact in-order associations and payload count.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable checker has no parent links, generic comparator, injected failure, stable handle, or concurrent state.

evidence: Reviewed rotation preconditions, order/ownership preservation, orientation classification from child balances, returned subtree-root reconnection, and metadata order.
Reviewed insertion bottom-up repair, deletion physical-removal path and continued ascent, and logarithmic path/rotation bounds.
Reviewed publication, iterator/reference identity, payload lifetime, serialization, and reclamation obligations.
proof_review.notes: Persistent, intrusive, parent-pointer, generic augmented, and concurrent variants retain implementation-specific proofs.

evidence: Original/academic AVL claims are separated from Boost.Intrusive, OCaml variant, Rust B-tree, and OpenJDK red-black implementation observations.
Worst-case height, insertion primitive-rotation count, deletion propagation, empirical performance, and API stability are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No cited production alternative is described as the executable classical AVL implementation.

evidence: The standard-library Python trace passed exact fifteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_avl_rotation_trace and verifies four insertion orientations plus deletion repair and global invariants.
All ten final source destinations and repository-local links were checked directly.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No named library tree, arbitrary comparator/payload, fault injection, parent/iterator contract, concurrent history, memory/cache profile, or benchmark was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed AVL/BST invariants, recurrence height proof, rotation algebra, insertion/deletion repair, metadata, identity/iteration, recursion/memory, concurrency, security, testing, and benchmarking.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed convention consistency, construct-before-link insertion, nonthrowing/transactional rotations, returned-root reconnect, delete-to-root propagation, child-balance equality, augmentation dependency order, handle matrix, depth/resource limits, invariant telemetry, serialization validation, and synchronized publication/reclamation.

pedagogical_review.notes: Builds logarithmic height from the minimum-node recurrence, derives rotations from ordered regions, distinguishes insertion and deletion propagation, includes reproduced LL/RR/LR/RL and deletion evidence, twelve misconceptions, ten examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, AVL/Boost/GNU/OCaml/Rust/OpenJDK maintainer, security, performance, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither generic comparator/exception/lifetime safety, stable handles, parent/augmentation correctness beyond the implemented height, recursion safety for corrupt input, thread safety, concurrent linearizability, safe reclamation, production memory/cache behavior, workload-independent superiority, certification, nor deployment fitness.
